g.title: g_envoy
g.text: Three GatewayClasses per cluster, each with its own
EnvoyProxy — but the one for home-ts is named ts.
Only TWO ClientTrafficPolicies, and neither is
named after a class: wildcard-lan covers Gateways
public and private whole, while wildcard-ts covers
ONE listener section of ts — so the other ts
listeners get no client-IP detection or timeouts.
The Gateways themselves are defined ONCE, in

g.title: r_listener
g.text: Check the listeners before adding a route
A route whose hostname matches no listener reports
nothing. The three tiers do not carry the same
hostname sets, so confirm against the live Gateway

g.title: r_trap
g.text: A ${CLUSTER_DOMAIN} route gets DNS FOR FREE the
moment it attaches to a gateway labelled
A ${COMMON_DOMAIN} name does NOT. It needs a
hand-written entry in the k8gb CNAME config, or the
route reports Accepted=True forever and never

g.title: x_auth
g.text: Tinyauth only proves WHO you are, then injects the
Authorization is a separate thing: each protected
route carries its own Envoy SecurityPolicy with
extAuth, defaultAction Deny and an explicit allow-list.
THERE IS NO CENTRAL ROLE MODEL. Access is per-route
and per-person, and visible in the manifest.

g.title: x_borrow
g.text: Robbinsdale and St. Petersburg reach it across the
tailnet rather than running a second copy, so their
protected routes depend on the overlay being up.
Tailnet-only routes lean on tailnet policy instead

g.title: x_tunnel
g.text: an outbound-only tunnel, so that site can publish
without an inbound port forward. A second ingress
path that bypasses the Envoy public tier entirely.
